chunks: Saad from al-Abbas ibn Musa from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abu Ayyub Ibrahim ibn Uthman al-Kazzaz from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him, 'How many are sufficient for the sighting of the crescent?' He said, 'Indeed, the month of Ramadan is an obligation from the obligations of Allah, so do not perform it based on conjecture. And the sighting of the crescent is not that a group stands and one says, "I have seen it," and the others say, "We have not seen it." If one sees it, it is as if a hundred have seen it; and if a hundred see it, it is as if a thousand have seen it. And it is not sufficient for the sighting of the crescent if there is no defect in the sky less than the testimony of fifty [witnesses]; and if there is a defect in the sky, the testimony of two men who enter and exit from a country is accepted.'
ai.seo_question: What is the required number of witnesses for sighting the crescent moon to begin Ramadan according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the evidentiary standards for moon sighting, emphasizing that a single credible witness suffices under clear skies, thereby preventing unnecessary delay in worship. It distinguishes between the high threshold of fifty witnesses required for exceptional cases (or two travelers in specific contexts) versus the standard acceptance of one witness, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of avoiding mere conjecture (*al-tazannun*) in establishing religious obligations.
